title: Bounded-above flat replacement on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and $N$ an integer. Every cochain complex $\mathcal F^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $\mathcal F^i=0$ for $i>N$ admits a bounded-above complex $\mathcal E^\bullet$ of flat $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], with $\mathcal E^i=0$ for $i>N$, and a termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] $\mathcal E^\bullet\to\mathcal F^\bullet$. These replacements can be chosen functorially for maps of bounded-above complexes.

source.place: Lemma 06YS (bounded-above flat replacement used in its proof)

proof.text: For a module sheaf $\mathcal M$, use the epimorphism of [lem-pc-sites-modules-quotient-j-shriek] indexed by all pairs $(U,s)$ with $s\in\mathcal M(U)$, whose summand map is adjoint to $1\mapsto s$; a module map $u:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'$ sends the $(U,s)$ summand to the $(U,u_U(s))$ summand, so these epimorphisms define a functorial $q_{\mathcal M}:Q(\mathcal M)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal M$. By [lem-pc-sites-modules-j-shriek-flat] each generator is flat, and by [lem-pc-sites-modules-coproduct-flat] the coproduct is flat. Set $\mathcal E^N=Q(\mathcal F^N)$ and descend. Having constructed $\mathcal E^{i+1}\to\mathcal F^{i+1}$ and its differential, form $P^i=\mathcal F^i\times_{\mathcal F^{i+1}}Z(\mathcal E^{i+1})$, where $Z(\mathcal E^{i+1})=\ker(d_{\mathcal E}^{i+1})$ maps to $\mathcal F^{i+1}$ through $\mathcal E^{i+1}\to\mathcal F^{i+1}$, and set $\mathcal E^i=Q(P^i)$. The maps through the two projections give $\mathcal E^i\to\mathcal F^i$ and $\mathcal E^i\to Z(\mathcal E^{i+1})\hookrightarrow\mathcal E^{i+1}$; hence $d_{\mathcal E}^{i+1}d_{\mathcal E}^i=0$ and the maps form a complex map. Inductively, $Z(\mathcal E^{i+1})\to Z(\mathcal F^{i+1})$ is epimorphic: for a cycle $z$ in $\mathcal F^{i+1}$, lift it through the preceding cycle-valued pullback, using that $d_{\mathcal F}z=0$. Therefore $P^i\to\mathcal F^i$ is epimorphic because $d_{\mathcal F}^if$ is a cycle and can be lifted to a cycle in $\mathcal E^{i+1}$. Thus each $\mathcal E^i\to\mathcal F^i$ is termwise epi; the construction is zero above $N$.

Let $\mathcal K^i=\ker(\mathcal E^i\to\mathcal F^i)$. The repaired pullback description shows that every cycle $\kappa\in Z(\mathcal K^{i+1})=\ker(d_{\mathcal E}^{i+1})\cap\ker(\mathcal E^{i+1}\to\mathcal F^{i+1})$ lifts along $\mathcal K^i\to Z(\mathcal K^{i+1})$: the pair $(0,\kappa)$ lies in $P^i$, and a lift through the epimorphism $\mathcal E^i\twoheadrightarrow P^i$ lies in $\mathcal K^i$ and maps to $\kappa$. Thus $\mathcal K^i\to Z(\mathcal K^{i+1})$ is surjective, so boundaries equal cycles and $H^i(\mathcal K)=0$. The short exact sequence of complexes and the definition of quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] then give that the termwise epimorphism $\mathcal E^\bullet\to\mathcal F^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 06YS, verification that the kernel is acyclic

proof.text: For a map of complexes $u:\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ with the same bound $N$, the indexed generator map sends the $(U,s)$ summand of $Q(\mathcal F^i)$ to the $(U,u^i_U(s))$ summand of $Q(\mathcal G^i)$ and commutes with the epimorphisms to the terms. Inductively, $u^i$ and the already constructed map in degree $i+1$ induce a map of the pullbacks $P^i(\mathcal F)\to P^i(\mathcal G)$; applying the same indexed construction gives $\mathcal E^i(\mathcal F)\to\mathcal E^i(\mathcal G)$. The pullback projections show compatibility with both differentials and augmentation maps. Thus the replacements and their quasi-isomorphisms are functorial.

lean.statement: theorem exists_functorial_boundedAbove_flat_replacement {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (N : ℤ) : let A := SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R) let P : ObjectProperty (CochainComplex A ℤ) := fun F => ∀ (i : ℤ), N < i → IsZero (F.X i) ∃ Q : P.FullSubcategory ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ, ∃ ε : Q ⟶ P.ι, ∀ F : P.FullSubcategory, (∀ (i : ℤ), SheafOfModules.IsFlat ((Q.obj F).X i)) ∧ (∀ (i : ℤ), N < i → IsZero ((Q.obj F).X i)) ∧ (∀ (i : ℤ), Epi ((ε.app F).f i)) ∧ QuasiIso (ε.app F)

reviewed_lean.note: site (C,J) small universe u, R : Sheaf J CommRingCat = O, Mod(O) via SheafOfModules of forget2 R; N : Z any sign; P = terms IsZero above N (landed inline bounded convention); IsFlat = recorded def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules; E zero above same N; Epi termwise = local surjectivity; Mathlib QuasiIso; functor Q on P.FullSubcategory + natural ε : Q -> P.ι = functoriality for maps with common bound N (node proof step 3)
